candidates.comment: Thanks for the detailed report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/321731, where a Codex installation also crashes vsce-sign 2.1.0 at `rdvl x0, #1`. Your Debian 13/OrbStack reproduction and successful macOS verification add useful environment coverage; the suggested .NET fix still needs confirmation with a rebuilt verifier.

Thanks for the request. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/306934, which requests enterprise-policy support for the same Disable AI Features setting. This report adds the Windows GPO requirement and the education-environment use case, where disabling agents alone still leaves AI UI visible.

Thanks for the report and the DevDrive example. Preserving temporarily unavailable folders in Recent is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/164491, including unmounted network shares and development drives. The VPN-at-startup scenario and the suggestion to offer “Remove From List” or “Cancel” are useful details to carry into that discussion.

Thanks for the report. This matches the macOS LAN-access regression tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328399, including Remote-SSH failing with “No route to host” while SSH from Terminal works. Your additional data point is VS Code 1.135.0 stable with Remote-SSH 0.126.0 on Apple Silicon failing to connect on port 2235, while Insiders succeeds; that comparison belongs with the ongoing investigation there.

Thanks for the context. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318358, whose discussion includes the native local harness, model/custom-agent parity, and sharing sessions between windows. This report adds useful emphasis on workbench context, VS Code and extension-provided tools, MCP configuration, integrated terminals, and clear backend labeling; local-model support through the CLI harness alone does not satisfy those requirements.

Thanks for the request. This is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317216: Claude Code sessions appear in the Sessions panel without a Delete option. The transcript-file workaround and Windows confirmations here provide additional context for that issue.

Thanks for the report. This is the same customization-row navigation problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/311200. That issue covers opening the clicked category rather than the previously selected section; this report adds that all customization options are affected.

Thanks for the report. This matches the title-persistence problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316994. This report adds Windows 11 Enterprise, VS Code 1.120.0, extension version 0.48.1, and repeated failures after reopening or continuing the conversation. A workaround reported there is to keep the conversation active and rename its item with the conversation list visible.

Thanks for the report. The same chat-saving error and loss of recent conversation history are tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/315161. This report adds a macOS 15.7.5 / VS Code 1.120.0 occurrence after more than an hour in agent mode, followed by a crash and missing history on restart.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/313334: renaming from the session list does not update the title immediately, and opening the conversation restores the original name. This report adds a Windows 1.120.0 reproduction where refreshing briefly reveals the renamed title before it reverts.

Thanks for the detailed report. The large-session save failure and missing history after restart are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/315161. This report adds useful evidence: the transcript remains on disk at about 51 MB / 73,370 lines, the same session recorded 55 session_start events, and extension-host responsiveness events occurred near the write failures.

Thanks for the detailed report and recovery steps. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/301793, which tracks chat history disappearing when an untitled workspace is saved, including after adding another folder. Your Windows 10 / VS Code 1.119.0 reproduction, the original folder retaining only the earlier conversation, and the storage-copy recovery details provide additional evidence for that issue. A fix is proposed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/305109 but has not merged.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/239798 already tracks a visible warning when malformed policy JSON cannot be applied. This report adds a concrete macOS example: extra quotation marks around the ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations array left the parsing failure discoverable only in logs, as shown in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/312534#issuecomment-4326631380.

Thanks for the report. The same missing Linux `pty.node` error from the Copilot SDK is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/300855, including reports from remote Linux hosts. This report adds Copilot Chat 0.43.0 on Windows-to-Linux Remote SSH, repeated remote extension-host crashes, and persistence after reinstalling; those details should remain part of the investigation there.

Thanks for the request. Local harness support in the Agents Window, including custom-agent integration, is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318358. This report adds the use case of analyzing large projects such as Unreal Engine, where you find the CLI harness insufficient; consolidating that feedback there does not mean the Local and CLI harnesses are equivalent.

Thanks for the report. The same unread-filter behavior across windows is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/291160. Your side-by-side demonstration provides another example of that issue; the expected behavior is to filter only the window where the control was clicked.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/291700 already tracks the same direct-storage coupling between the title-bar control and sessions filter. Consolidating there should retain this proposal for a shared service or injected filter, including the cross-window coordination concern highlighted by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/291911.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/286797 already tracks the same cloud-session problem: the original prompt is replaced by “Initial Implementation.” This report adds https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/291354 as a concrete example, with the original prompt and extra instructions available in the PR body, plus the explanation that the fallback appears when the API omits the problem statement.

Thanks for the report. This matches the cloud-agent Stop/cancellation failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/269158. This report adds that stopping from the chat editor leaves the agent view spinning and that reloading still shows the cloud agent running; those observations should remain part of the cancellation investigation.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/213520 already includes this exact sequence: forwarding works on the initial connection, then opening a workspace leaves the terminal using an invalid agent socket and ssh-add fails. Consolidating there also preserves your Windows-to-Linux setup, the failure continuing across reconnections, and your observation that removing the remote server installation temporarily restores forwarding.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/204712 already tracks an option to skip collapsed lines in Find without expanding folded regions. Your renewed interest in the earlier request at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/168701 can be consolidated there; you can add a 👍 reaction to the open request's description.

Thanks for the request. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/202957, which tracks moving a workspace while preserving its state, including opened tabs and Copilot chat history. This report also specifies selecting a new folder location and retaining window layout and cached workspace data.

Thanks for the report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/154913, where the discussion explicitly notes that automatic match updates do not scroll off-screen results into view. This report adds a useful distinction: the match index advances correctly, but revealing it requires navigating to the next match and back, observed on macOS 12.6.2 with VS Code 1.76.1.

Thanks for the report. The same notebook-outline exception is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/283679, which includes reproduction steps involving rapid edits to the Chat Log Notebook. This telemetry report adds the refresh path through NotebookOutlineDataSource.recomputeActive and outline tree updates; that diagnostic detail belongs with the same investigation.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/101064 already tracks changing the font family and size of the editor Find/Replace inputs. Your example of capital `I` and lowercase `l` being difficult to distinguish is a useful readability requirement for that work.

Thanks for the detailed report. The same Find Next Selection defect is tracked at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/300085, with a proposed fix in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/300086. This report adds a Linux snap reproduction where moving the cursor without selecting text changes the search term, and confirms that the never setting is affected too; those details should remain part of the fix's scope.

Thanks for the report. The editor freezing while evaluating a regex is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/30874, including a Windows report where pasting a C-comment regex hangs the window. This report adds the expression `\/\*([^*]|\*+[^/])*\*\/` on VS Code 1.85.1, Windows 10 x64, while using Ctrl+H in a C file.

Thanks for the reproduction. This is the editor Find regex-blocking problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/30874. This report adds a pinned terminal recording fixture and the exact trigger—completing `\[.+,.+,.+,\]`—plus the non-freezing alternative `\[([^,]+,){3}[^,]+\]`.

Thanks for the request. Configurable find/replace fonts are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/101064, including monospace fonts for regex readability. Your example of distinguishing `{}` and `()` in long expressions adds useful context; the configurable-font option you suggested fits that existing request.

Thanks for the report. The Arabic text reordering when using Ctrl+F is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/233573. Your mixed Arabic/English Markdown sample, selecting a whole RTL word before opening Find, and Fedora Snap environment provide additional reproduction details for that issue.

Thanks for the report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/48123, which discusses punctuation ordering in Sort Lines Ascending and includes the same quoted-prefix behavior. This report adds a useful double-quoted JSON example: "abc-def" sorts before "abc", although the unquoted values sort in the opposite order.

Thanks for the report. The active-file ranking regression is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/307605. This report adds useful reproduction details across agent/ask/plan modes on Windows 11, particularly the difficulty finding the active file among identically named Next.js page.tsx files.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/93470 already tracks distinguishing Explorer-triggered file events from workspace-edit-triggered events, including onWillRenameFiles. Consolidating there should retain this Java class-and-file rename example, where applying the refactoring triggers another rename calculation, and the alternative suggested here of suppressing events for edits originating from onWill listeners.

Thanks for clarifying the example. Automatic suggestions while editing inside an existing word are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/33591. Your `funcstart` example, GIFs, and confirmation that Ctrl+Space works capture why manual triggering does not satisfy this request.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/162455 already tracks native TODO diagnostic classification and filtering TODOs independently from other Problems, including the Dart analyzer case. Your specific request for a Show TODOs toggle alongside Show Infos belongs with that work; !todo remains a text-filter workaround, not a replacement for the requested category.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/105487 already tracks invoking extension commands from the CLI with multiple arguments, including execution in an existing VS Code window. This report also highlights scripting and flexible argument values; those requirements belong in the same discussion.

Thanks for the context. The same bucket-first completion flow is already proposed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/249249: choose a file, symbol, or tool prefix, then see suggestions scoped to that type. Consolidating there should also preserve your recent-file shortcuts, Backspace return to the top level, and the JSON-symbol noise reported in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/270430.

Thanks for clarifying the interaction requirement. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/135114 already tracks clickable padding before the first character, including your earlier explanation there, so this can be consolidated with that request.

The important details from this report are that clicking the padding should place the cursor at column one and dragging right should select part of the line. Visual-only CSS spacing and line-number or keyboard workarounds do not fully cover those interactions.

Thanks for the context. The remaining URI-backed terminal selection and preview work is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/287867. This report adds useful labeling examples for a range within one command (`ls:5-10`) and across commands (`ls:5-npm run build:10`); those should inform the design there.

Thanks for the report and the renderer investigation. Inline newline and CR/LF markers are already requested in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/12223, including the expectation that editor.renderControlCharacters should show them. Consolidating there preserves this report's Windows reproduction, the concern about the setting's description, and your source investigation at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/26646#issuecomment-2490997272; this does not mean the capability has been implemented.

Thanks for the request. Persistent undo/redo across restarts is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/15135, where the discussion explicitly includes persisting undo stacks across all editors. This report adds substantial support for retaining both undo and redo for saved code files after restarting; `files.restoreUndoStack` currently covers reopening files within a session, and Local History is not equivalent to preserving that edit stack.

Thanks for the report. ARM64 Snap availability is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/125120, which remains open until the ARM64 channels are actually published. This report adds the Ubuntu 20.04 ARM64 installation error and the suggestion to investigate Canonical's remote ARM build service; those details belong with that work. The available deb package does not replace the requested Snap Store support.

Thanks for the request. The same native Backspace behavior—removing an indented whitespace-only line and returning to the previous line's end—is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/42785. Consolidating there; this thread also contributes reports that Hungry Delete can disable Backspace until a reload or delay/freeze when suggestions appear, reinforcing the request for native support.

Thanks for the request. This is already tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/74342, including the same case where a custom code-editor background also changes Settings and extension information pages. Your additional example of Jupyter Interactive windows is useful context for that separation; the requested editor.codeBackground name is one possible approach to the same capability.

Thanks for the detailed examples. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/27905 already tracks both Ctrl+click whole-word selection and Ctrl+drag selection that snaps to word boundaries. This report adds a useful demonstration (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bfyO8haWKfg) and explains why double-click dragging does not replace the continuous Ctrl-held select-copy-paste workflow; those details remain relevant to that request.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/30191 already includes configurable sizing across all scrollbars and global horizontal/vertical defaults. Consolidating there, with this report's explicit requirement that component-specific settings inherit the global size unless overridden.

Thanks for the detailed report. This is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/13516, including the case where not all document lines are visible. Your Linux reproduction, the lack of recalculation on save, and the decoration-removal case provide useful additional detail for that request.

Thanks for the request. This capability is also tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/107989: matching the embedded language at the cursor rather than only the document-level editorLangId. This report adds a concrete use case worth retaining there: formatting selected Vue HTML with extension.formatSelectionAsHtml, including matching HTML regions with =~ /html/.

Thanks for the context. Touch-based editor text selection is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/47770, whose discussion explicitly includes Remote Desktop in Touch mode. This report adds Surface Pro X pen/stylus use and iPad Remote Desktop observations, including unsuccessful double-tap and Shift-plus-arrow selection, which are useful cases to retain there.

Thanks for the detailed examples. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/16998 tracks indentation-aware navigation to blank lines with both the mouse and arrow keys, covering your second proposed solution without requiring automatic whitespace cleanup to be disabled. Your alternative of preserving whitespace-only lines is also tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/209939.

Thanks for the request. Extensions can already render gutter icons with `gutterIconPath` and contribute right-click actions through `editor/lineNumber/context`, but those do not provide direct click actions on their decorations. That remaining capability is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/224134, including coexistence with breakpoints and overlapping icons; this thread also contributes the bookmark-click use case and the concern about which decoration receives interaction.

Thanks for the request. Touch-drag text selection is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/47770. Your Windows proposal adds a useful interaction option: start horizontally to select or vertically to scroll, then retain that mode even if the drag changes direction. Consolidating there keeps that proposal with the other touch-selection designs.

Thanks for the report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/11809, which tracks moving consecutive lines with multiple cursors without losing cursors or moving only the primary line. Your Windows 7 reproduction using Ctrl+Alt+Down followed by Alt+Up, and the unmerged implementation attempt at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/48406, provide additional context for that work.

Thanks for the report. The missing remote VS Code IPC socket error is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/157275, which also includes Python browser-opening failures. This report adds the LangGraph development trigger after updating to VS Code 1.132.0, with Windows connecting to Ubuntu and an ENOENT error under /run/user/4100/.

Thanks for the report. The chat-saving error and stack match https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/315161, which tracks this serialization failure. Consolidating there preserves your additional report of macOS Tahoe 26.4.1 and more than ten crashes in one day; the supplied stack identifies the saving failure but does not establish what caused those crashes.

Thanks for the detailed report and sample files. This is the same size-dependent regex Replace All defect tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237975: negated character classes can unexpectedly span newlines on the large-replacement path. This report adds the Windows 10 reproduction with extensions disabled and the specific case where ^([^\t<]+).*$ replaced with $1 clears a following </odstavec> line; those examples should be retained when addressing the shared defect.
